VYseisties are perfectly delicious when served plain, without added fla-

vorings. Or you can season them with herbs, spices, garlic, and onion.
Whatever you do, carefully cook vegetables just until they are tender-crisp
and still flavorful. Limp, overcooked veggies lose their appeal as well as
some of their nutrients.

Most vegetables contain negligible amounts of protein and fat but offer
carbohydrate, fiber, and abundant vitamins and minerals. Eating vegetables
is an excellent way to boost your vitamin intake—and is preferable to taking
vitamin pills. These “all-natural vitamins” work synergistically with other
phytochemicals found in food to protect your health.

The first five recipes offer basic advice about cooking methods. Because
you will choose your own vegetable combinations in the earlier recipes,
nutrition information is provided only for the remaining recipes. Refer to
tables 1.2 and table 4.1 for additional nutrition information.
